ratios.name: Skull length / standing hip-joint height
ratios.definition: Total skull length (premaxilla to quadrate or occiput) divided by acetabulum height above the ground in a standing pose
ratios.basis: Skulls: FMNH PR 2081 ~1.39-1.40 m (WIKI_SUE 1.394; CARR2020 >=1.4), BHI 3033 ~1.40 m (HS2003), MOR 555 mount 1.20 m (PAD2022). Hips: straight-limb leg lengths 3.300/3.068/3.055 m (H2011) give 0.42/0.46/0.39. Standing acetabulum heights derived from B2009 coordinates (BHI 3033 3.11 m, MOR 555 2.67 m) give 0.45/0.45. The HG2002 running pose (2.5 m) with the MOR skull gives 0.48. If hip height is taken to the top of the ilium (FM 13 ft = 3.96 m) the value is about 0.35.

ratios.name: Skull length / femur length
ratios.definition: Total skull length divided by maximum femur length
ratios.basis: Total length: FMNH 1.394/1.321 = 1.06; BHI 3033 1.40/1.350 = 1.04 (1.40/1.278 = 1.10 with the H2011 femur); MOR 555 mount 1.20/1.30 = 0.92. Using GE2017 head length (to the posterior parietal margin, about 8-9% shorter): FMNH 0.97, BHI 3033 0.94-0.99, MOR 980 1.04, RTMP 81.6.1 0.97, with femora from P2020 Table 1.

ratios.name: Skull width at rear / skull length
ratios.definition: Width across the quadrates (jaw joints) divided by skull length
ratios.basis: GE2017 Table 1 width/length: FMNH PR 2081 0.71, MOR 008 0.69, LACM 23844 0.65, MOR 980 0.64, BHI 3033 0.61, RTMP 81.6.1 0.60, BHI 4100 0.53 (median 0.64). PAD2022 MOR 555 mount 0.60/1.20 = 0.50. Against total skull length: FMNH 0.902/1.394 = 0.65; BHI 3033 0.772/1.40 = 0.55. HS2003 describes T. rex as 'extremely broad posteriorly' compared with Tarbosaurus but gives no width.

ratios.name: Skull depth / skull length
ratios.definition: Maximum skull height (through the postorbital bar) divided by length (premaxilla to quadrate condyle)
ratios.basis: Inverse of published L/H ratios (CARR2020S1): FMNH 2.3 gives 0.435, UWBM 99000 2.6 gives 0.385, AMNH 5027 3.1 gives 0.32. Carr's adult category is L/H 2.3-2.6 (0.385-0.435). HS2003 BHI 3033 57/140 = 0.41 (Tarbosaurus 0.39). Juveniles have L/H >=3.0 (<=0.33).

ratios.name: Tibia / femur length
ratios.definition: Maximum tibia length divided by maximum femur length (adults)

ratios.name: Metatarsal III / femur length
ratios.definition: Metatarsal III length divided by femur length
ratios.basis: PC2016 Table 2: MOR 555 0.523, CM 9380 0.536, RTMP 81.12.1 0.542, BHI 6230 0.600 (smaller adult); juvenile LACM 23845 0.616. A typical adult femur:tibia:MT III is about 1 : 0.90 : 0.53. MT III was not verified for FMNH PR 2081.

ratios.name: Lower leg (tibia + MT III) / femur
ratios.definition: Sum of tibia and metatarsal III lengths divided by femur length

ratios.name: Leg (pelvic limb) length / body length
ratios.definition: H2011 skeletal 'leg length' divided by skeletal head-to-tail length
ratios.basis: H2011 Table 3: CM 0.256, BHI 3033 0.260, MOR 555 0.263, FMNH 0.269; juvenile Jane 0.329. The text gives limb/total length falling from 33% to 26% through ontogeny. This is not standing hip height.

ratios.name: Standing hip-joint height / body length
ratios.definition: Acetabulum height in a standing or mid-stance pose divided by skeletal body length
ratios.basis: Derived: B2009 BHI 3033 hip 3.11 m / 11.78 m (H2011) = 0.264; B2009 MOR 555 2.67 / 11.60 = 0.230; HG2002 flexed running pose 2.5 / 11.60 = 0.216. Mixes model and skeletal sources.

ratios.name: Shoulder-to-hip (gleno-acetabular) distance / body length
ratios.definition: Distance between approximate glenoid and acetabulum centres divided by body length
ratios.basis: H2011 Table 3: BHI 3033 0.211, CM 0.212, FMNH 0.225. MOR 555 0.157 was flagged anomalous by the authors; juvenile 0.178. Derived adult GAD is 2.49-2.77 m.

ratios.name: Tail length / body length
ratios.definition: Tail from the first free caudal to the tip divided by head-to-tail length
ratios.basis: H2011 Table 3: FMNH 0.512 (reconstructed beyond caudal 27), MOR 555 0.551, BHI 3033 0.594. CM 0.470 was flagged as reconstructed; juvenile 0.599. The text says the tail stays at about 60% of body length through ontogeny. Derived adult tails are 6.3-7.0 m.

ratios.name: Femur length / body length
ratios.definition: Femur length divided by skeletal body length
ratios.basis: Derived from H2011 Table 3: CM 0.106, FMNH 0.107, BHI 3033 0.108, MOR 555 0.110; juvenile 0.122.

ratios.name: Skull length / body length
ratios.definition: Total skull length divided by skeletal body length

ratios.name: Chest (ribcage) width / body length
ratios.definition: Maximum skeletal ribcage or gastral width divided by body length
ratios.basis: PAD2022: MOR 555 mount ribcage 'well over a meter wide' (>1.0/11.60 = >0.086). FM_MAKEOVER: first gastral pair 44 in (1.12 m) tip to tip / 12.29 m = 0.091; this is a gastral span, not maximum rib width. No published fleshed body width was found. B2009 adds about 18% of half-width as soft tissue lateral to the ribs. Upper value left open.

ratios.name: Glenoid spacing / skull width at jaw joints
ratios.definition: Horizontal distance between the shoulder sockets divided by skull width at the jaw joints
ratios.basis: PAD2022 MOR 555 mount: 68/60 cm. Glenoid spacing / body length is about 0.68/11.60 = 0.059. Single mount; the coracoids may be slightly too close because no furcula was recovered.

ratios.name: Neck length (along S-curve) / skull length
ratios.definition: Sum of the three neck-segment lengths divided by skull length
ratios.basis: PAD2022 MOR 555 mount: (45 + 75 + 60) / 120 cm. Single reconstructed mount. The snout tip is only 135 cm in front of the glenoid in this S-posture.

ratios.name: Humerus / femur length
ratios.definition: Humerus length divided by femur length
ratios.basis: PAD2022: humerus 37 cm / femur 130 cm (same mount) = 0.285; /1.280 m (MOR 555 femur, H2011 and P2020) = 0.289. Ulna 20 cm, manual digit I 22 cm, digit II 25 cm. Only one specimen.

ratios.name: Scapulocoracoid length / femur length
ratios.definition: Scapulocoracoid length divided by femur length
ratios.basis: PAD2022 MOR 555 mount: 127/130 cm.

ratios.name: Ilium length / femur length
ratios.definition: Ilium length divided by femur length (sets pelvis length)

ratios.name: Foot (footprint, about digit III plus pad) length / hip height
ratios.definition: Footprint length (proxy for pedal digit III length +5%, as in MC2014) divided by hip height
ratios.basis: MC2014 tyrannosaurid: 0.579/2.87 = 0.20; Alexander's assumption h = 4 FL gives 0.25. T. rex tracks of 0.96-1.0 m (F2026), 0.86 m (Tyrannosauripus) and 0.72 m (Manning 2008) against hip 3.1-3.3 m give 0.22-0.32. F2026 says tracks overestimate the foot; an 0.8 m foot gives 0.24-0.26.

ratios.name: Footprint width / footprint length
ratios.definition: Track width divided by track length
ratios.basis: F2026 R2 0.80/0.96 = 0.83; MC2014 Bellatoripes mean 51.9/57.9 = 0.90; Tyrannosauripus 64/86 = 0.74 (width only from Wikipedia, unverified).

ratios.name: Pace width / footprint length
ratios.definition: Lateral distance between left and right track centroids, perpendicular to the direction of travel, divided by footprint length
ratios.basis: Derived from the published pace angulation and stride. F2026: PA 164-167° and stride ~4 m give pace 2.01-2.02 m and pace width 0.23-0.28 m; /0.96 m = 0.24-0.29. MC2014 trackway A: paces 174/173 cm and stride 346 cm give 13.2 cm; /57.9 cm = 0.23. Rounding the stride by +/-0.5 cm moves this between 0 and 19 cm.

ratios.name: Pace width / hip height
ratios.definition: Lateral spacing of left and right foot centroids divided by hip height

ratios.name: External trackway width / hip height
ratios.definition: Width between lines bounding the lateral track edges divided by hip height
ratios.basis: F2026: 0.8-1.0 m against hip 3.1-4.0 m. External width / footprint length = 0.83-1.04; the published midline overlap is 40-50%.

ratios.name: Pace angulation (degrees)
ratios.definition: Angle at a footprint between lines to the preceding and following contralateral prints (180° = single file)
ratios.basis: F2026 adult T. rex trackway: about 164° and 167° (published). MC2014 Bellatoripes: the text says 'nearing 180°' but Table 1 prints 117°; recomputing from pace and stride gives about 171° (168-180° within rounding).

ratios.name: Relative stride length (stride / hip height)
ratios.definition: Stride (successive prints of the same foot) divided by hip height
ratios.basis: VB2021: stride 3.88 m (2 x 1.94) / 3.1 m = 1.25, and the published statement that bipedal dinosaurs seem to prefer about 1.3. MC2014: 346/287 = 1.21 (346/230 = 1.50 with flexed h). F2026: 4 m / 3.1-3.3 m = 1.2-1.3 (1.0 with h = 4 m). MC2014 also prints lambda/h = 1.69, which could not be reproduced.

ratios.name: Total toe divarication II-IV in tracks (degrees)
ratios.definition: Sum of the interdigital angles II-III and III-IV
ratios.basis: F2026 T. rex R2: 35 + 40 = 75° (published). MC2014 Bellatoripes 51-80° (trackway A mean 64°, B and C 70°). III-IV exceeds II-III in both.

ratios.name: COM cranial distance from hip / femur length
ratios.definition: Horizontal distance of the whole-body COM in front of the hip joint divided by femur length
ratios.basis: H2011 gives about 30-45% of femur length as the most plausible adult range, with Sue at 44-61% (published). Minimal models (Table 7): CM 43.4%, BHI 3033 41.0%, MOR 555 44.7%, Sue 66.8%, Jane 35.0%. B2009 best estimates are 0.47-0.57 m (0.37-0.45 femur lengths).

ratios.name: COM depth below hip / femur length
ratios.definition: Vertical distance of the COM below the hip joint divided by femur length
ratios.basis: H2011 text: 22-35% (CM, MOR 555), 26-28% (Sue), 38-50% (BHI 3033, possibly a modelling error). Minimal models: 26.2, 25.5, 38.7, 26.3%. B2009: 0.30-0.33 m below the hip.

ratios.name: Head mass / body mass
ratios.definition: Head segment mass fraction
ratios.basis: H2011 Table 4: CM 0.053, Sue 0.041, BHI 3033 0.065, MOR 555 0.111 (inflated by scan quality), Jane 0.058. B2009: 0.089 (BHI 3033), 0.107 (MOR 555). Typical is the median of the adult values.

ratios.name: Tail mass / body mass
ratios.definition: Tail segment mass fraction
ratios.basis: H2011 minimal models 0.099 (BHI 3033) to 0.207 (MOR 555), Sue 0.123 (maximal models up to 0.221). B2009: 0.144 (BHI 3033), 0.178 (MOR 555).

ratios.name: One hind limb mass / body mass
ratios.definition: Mass of a single leg (thigh + shank + metatarsus + pes) divided by whole-body mass
ratios.basis: B2009 Table 9 best estimates 0.144 (BHI 3033) and 0.160 (MOR 555), sensitivity extremes 0.098-0.224 (published). The H2011 limb rows sum with the axial rows to the whole-body mass, which implies both legs combined, giving about 0.095-0.13 per leg (derived; see open questions).

ratios.name: Preferred walking Froude number v^2/(g*h)
ratios.definition: Dimensionless speed for routine walking, with h = hip height
ratios.basis: VB2021: 1.28 (0.80-1.64) m/s at h 3.1 m gives 0.054 (0.021-0.088). F2026: 1.5-2 m/s at h 3.1 m gives 0.07-0.13 (0.065-0.10 at h 4 m). The smaller Bellatoripes trackmakers (MC2014) give 0.11-0.25.

ratios.name: Maximum walking (walk-run limit) Froude number
ratios.definition: Froude number at the highest bone-stress-permissible speed
ratios.basis: S2017: Fr = 1.0 at a 100 MPa peak-stress limit. HG2002: Fr = 1 gives about 5 m/s for h ~2.5 m. At h = 3.1 m, Fr = 1 corresponds to about 5.5 m/s.

ratios.name: Preferred step frequency at full scale (Hz)
ratios.definition: Steps per second at the preferred walking speed
ratios.basis: VB2021: tail natural frequency interpreted as preferred step frequency for RGM.792.000 (hip 3.1 m, step 1.94 m). Under dynamic similarity the frequency scales with 1/sqrt(hip height).

ratios.name: Soft tissue lateral to ribs / one-side trunk width
ratios.definition: Fleshing rule: soft-tissue thickness outside the rib heads as a fraction of the half-width of the body
ratios.basis: B2009 MOR 555 best-estimate model: 60 mm = 17.8% of one side's mediolateral width; a 'similar ratio' was used in all their best-estimate models.

ratios.name: Foot rotation toward midline (degrees)
ratios.definition: Angle of the digit III axis relative to the direction of travel; positive = toed-in
ratios.basis: MC2014 Bellatoripes: trackway A +6, -9 (pathological outward), +5 (mean +2); trackway C +12, +20. The diagnosis says 'slight inward rotation of pes towards midline'. Not available for the F2026 T. rex trackway.

ratios.name: Vertical hip excursion amplitude / hip height (walking)
ratios.definition: Amplitude of hip or tail-base vertical motion during pendular walking divided by hip height
ratios.basis: Derived from VB2021: 0.08 m amplitude for 1.94 m steps at 3.1 m hip height in their simulation.

ratios.name: Foot-placement offset from midline / thigh offset from midline
ratios.definition: Half the trackway pace width divided by the lateral offset of the thigh segment CM in mounted-skeleton models
ratios.basis: Trackway half pace-widths of 0.066-0.14 m (F2026, MC2014) against B2009 thigh CM offsets of 0.363-0.408 m. Indicates strong medial (adducted) foot placement while walking.

posture_findings: [PUBLISHED] Limb posture at mid-stance. Gatesy et al. 2009 restricted T. rex to 'a narrow region of neither very columnar nor very flexed poses'. Hutchinson et al. 2005: 'more upright (although not completely columnar) poses are more plausible'. Hutchinson 2004: larger theropods used 'fairly upright limb orientations'. Hutchinson et al. 2007: because the CM lies cranial to the hip, T. rex 'did not stand or move with extremely columnar, elephantine limbs. It required some flexion in the limbs to stand still.' [INTERPRETIVE] For the robot: moderately flexed knee and ankle with the femur angled forward of vertical, not straight pillar legs.

[PUBLISHED + DERIVED] Standing hip height compared with skeletal leg length. HG2002's running-pose model (MOR 555 limb bones) had a hip height of about 2.5 m against a skeletal leg length of 3.055 m (H2011), a ratio of 0.82. MC2014: flexing the knee to 110° and the ankle to 140° lowers the hip to 0.80 of the straight-limb value (2.30 vs 2.87 m). From B2009 coordinates (whole-body CM height plus CM depth below the hip), the BHI 3033 cast mount has its acetabulum at about 3.11 m, close to leg length 3.068 m (a near-columnar mount pose), and MOR 555 at about 2.67 m (0.87 of leg length). VB2021 used 3.1 m for 'Trix'.

[PUBLISHED] Centre of mass. H2011 minimal models put the COM 0.52-0.80 m in front of and 0.32-0.50 m below the hip (Sue 0.80 m and -0.355 m). The most plausible adult range is ~30-45% of femur length forward (Sue 44-61%). B2009 best estimates: 0.47-0.57 m forward and 0.30-0.33 m below; 'the CM remained in front and below the hip joint in all models'. [INTERPRETIVE] During single support the stance foot must sit under or slightly ahead of the hip. Trunk pitch and tail mass are the main ways to trim balance.

[DERIVED from B2009 coordinates] Body attitude in digital models of mounted skeletons, relative to the acetabulum: head CM about 3.80 m forward and +0.23 m (BHI 3033) to +0.40 m (MOR 555) above; neck CM 2.7-2.9 m forward, +0.26 to +0.44 m; thorax CM 1.3-1.6 m forward, -0.05 to -0.15 m; tail CM 1.9-2.3 m behind, -0.02 to -0.30 m. So the vertebral column is near-horizontal, the head is carried at or slightly above hip level, and the tail is held roughly level. SN2019 places the axial-body CM about 3.8 m behind the snout tip.

[PUBLISHED] Neck shape. PAD2022 (MOR 555-based UCMP mount): an S-shaped neck with a 45 cm anterior horizontal section, a 75 cm middle diagonal section and a 60 cm posterior horizontal section; the snout tip is 135 cm in front of the glenoid. Snively & Russell 2007 (ZJLS): 'the strong dorsally convex curvature of the neck from C1 to C5 placed the neural spine of C4 at the highest point of the neck', with a bird-like posterior U-curve. Snively & Russell 2007 (Anat Rec abstract): m. transversospinalis capitis 'probably filled in the posterior dorsal concavity of the neck, for a more crocodilian- than avian-like profile'. [INTERPRETIVE] Give the robot an S-curved neck axis under a smooth, muscle-filled dorsal outline.

[PUBLISHED] Neck function (Snively & Russell 2007, Anat Rec abstract). Tyrannosaurus had relatively large moment arms for lateroflexion and dorsiflexion and large dorsiflexor origin areas. It was 'not particularly specialized for neck ventro-flexion', which is consistent with 'puncture-and-pull and powerful shake feeding'. [INTERPRETIVE] Emphasise head-lift and side-sweep degrees of freedom.

[PUBLISHED, head pitch SECONDARY] Head orientation. Stevens 2006 abstract: binocular fields 45-60° wide in Tyrannosaurus and other coelurosaurs, compared with about 20° in Allosaurus and Carcharodontosaurus, so the eyes face substantially forward. Stevens' web page reports that his study and Witmer & Ridgely's semicircular-canal CT 'independently suggest that T. rex habitually would have held its head dipped 5-10 degrees downward'.

[PUBLISHED] Skull silhouette. HS2003: 'the skull of T. rex is extremely broad posteriorly but narrows towards the snout'; Tarbosaurus is narrower. CARR2020: adult skull L/H is 2.3-2.6, against >=3.0 in juveniles. GE2017: width across the quadrates is 0.53-0.71 of head length. The overall shape is a deep, broad-backed head with a narrowing snout.

[PUBLISHED] Forelimbs and shoulders. The 2018 Field Museum remount corrected SUE's furcula and adjusted the scapulae, which 'lowered SUE's arms and brought them forward a bit. Now, they look as though they could actually touch each other.' BR2003: the scapulocoracoids 'would probably not have met at the midline, but would nonetheless have closely approached each other'. LC2008: furcula placement shows the coracoids were close together. PAD2022: glenoids 68 cm apart, humerus 37 cm against a 130 cm femur; the hands could not reach the mouth or, by his analysis, each other. B2009: the lateral body outline passes under the scapulocoracoids and probably not below the arms.

[PUBLISHED] Belly and gastralia. FM 2018: the gastral basket was added (26 of about 60 elements), 'with the first pair stretching 44 inches apart at the tips', the ribs were widened, and the skeleton became 'bigger than before'. Makovicky: T. rex was 'very barrel-chested'. BR2003: gastralia extensively fused anteriorly. PAD2022: ribcage 'well over a meter wide'. B2009: the belly outline 'passes close to the pelvis (ischium and pubis) even with the knee slightly flexed', with modest flesh below the gastral plane.

[PUBLISHED] Hip and femur orientation. BR2003: with the femoral shaft vertical, the head slopes dorsomedially, so 'the femur probably projected ventrolaterally from the hip rather than directly ventrally'. STV2008: the 'axislike insertion of the femur head within acetabulum suggests little femoral abduction was possible'. [INTERPRETIVE] Place the knees slightly outboard of the hips and bring the feet back toward the midline through the shank and metatarsus.

[PUBLISHED] Tail. Skeletal tail length is about 51-59% of total length in adults (H2011 Table 3; about 60% in the text). SUE was mounted with 47 caudals (BR2003) and the tail is reconstructed beyond caudal 27 (H2011). M. caudofemoralis longus is 162-192 kg per side in minimal models (H2011, 2.0-3.2% of body mass) and 261 kg for BHI 3033 in Persons & Currie 2011 (quoted by H2011). PC2011: deepened hemal arches enlarged the CFL. VB2021: the tail was suspended passively by interspinous ligaments that store elastic energy. [INTERPRETIVE] Use a deep, heavy tail base and treat the tail as a counterweight and spring.

[PUBLISHED] Resting posture (STV2008, 'Rex, sit'). T. rex could lower itself onto the pubic boot, with knees and boot touching the ground together because the ventral surface of the boot sits just below the knee. It probably rose by tipping forward onto the pubis, using the forelimbs as anchors, and lifting the rump first.

[PUBLISHED] Mass and its distribution. Adults were about 6000-8000 kg and Sue about 9500 kg (H2011 abstract, minimal models; whole-body density about 840-890 kg/m3). Other estimates: B2009 6072-7655 kg; S2017 7207 kg (BHI 3033); SN2019 6987 and 9131 kg; P2020 femoral-circumference estimates 8462 kg (Sue) and 8870 kg (Scotty, +/-25%); FM 'nine or ten tons'. H2011 minimal-model fractions: head 4.1-11.1%, neck 3.2-7.3%, torso 54-59% (MOR 35% anomalous), tail 10-21%, forelimbs 0.1-0.4%. B2009: each hind limb 14.4-16.0%.

[PUBLISHED] Choosing an adult exemplar. H2011: limb length as a share of total length fell from 33% in the juvenile 'Jane' to 26% in adults, the torso lengthened (about +3% GAD/body length), and tail length stayed near 60%. CARR2020: juveniles have long, low skulls. P2020: robust 'Scotty' likely had 'a shorter total hip height and snout-vent length than other known specimens showing more elongate proportions'. [INTERPRETIVE] For a recognisable adult T. rex, use adult proportions (Sue, Stan, MOR 555), not 'Jane'.
gauge_and_gait_findings: [PUBLISHED] Falkingham et al. 2026 describe the first trackway likely made by an adult T. rex (Hell Creek Formation, North Dakota, ~66.5 Ma). Four tracks span about 7 m. Tracks are about 0.9-1.0 m long and 0.6-0.8 m wide. Track R2 is 0.96 x 0.80 m, with digit II/III/IV impressions of 34/47/30 cm (tip to hypex), about 13 cm wide, and interdigital angles of 35° (II-III) and 40° (III-IV). Stride is about 4 m and external trackway width about 0.8-1.0 m; tracks 'significantly overlap with the midline by 40-50%'. Pace angulation is about 167° (L1-R1-L2) and 164° (R1-L2-R2). Estimated speed is about 1.5-2 m/s, which the authors call only 'roughly indicative'.

[DERIVED] From the F2026 pace angulation and stride: pace is about 2.01-2.02 m and the lateral distance between left and right track centroids is about 0.23-0.28 m. That is 0.24-0.29 footprint lengths and about 0.07-0.09 of a 3.1-3.3 m hip height. External width minus track width (0.8-1.0 m minus 0.6-0.8 m) gives the same order, about 0.2 m. An adult T. rex therefore walked with nearly in-line, narrow-gauge foot placement.

[PUBLISHED] McCrea et al. 2014, Bellatoripes fredlundi (tyrannosaurid, likely Albertosaurus, Gorgosaurus or Daspletosaurus, not T. rex). The diagnosis reads 'Trackway narrow with slight inward rotation of pes towards midline' and 'Footprints in trackway are in line, with a pace angulation nearing 180°. Trackway width is narrow, with footprints overlapping the midline'. Trackway A: footprint length 52.3-62.0 cm (mean 57.9), paces 174 and 173 cm, stride 346 cm, foot rotation -9° to +6°. No metatarsal impressions. Hip height is 2.87 m from a tyrannosaurid regression (2.80 m general; 2.30 m with knee 110° and ankle 140°). Speed is 6.40-8.50 km/h.

[DERIVED; possible error] McCrea 2014 Table 1 prints a pace angulation of 117° for trackway A. That contradicts the text ('nearing 180°') and the tabulated paces and stride, which by the law of cosines give about 171° (168-180° for +/-0.5 cm rounding). 117° is probably a transposition of 171°. The derived pace width is about 13 cm (0-19 cm), roughly 0.23 footprint lengths and 0.05 of the 2.87 m hip height.

[DERIVED/INTERPRETIVE] Static models place the feet much wider apart than trackways do. In B2009's mounted-skeleton models the segment CMs sit about 0.36-0.41 m (thigh), 0.30-0.42 m (metatarsus) and 0.45-0.46 m (digit III) from the midline, so the feet are about 0.6-0.9 m apart. Trackway centroids are only about 0.07-0.14 m either side of the midline. When walking, T. rex therefore put each foot close under the body midline. A robot that stands with its feet under its hips must swing each foot medially at touchdown to leave a recognisably T. rex trackway, which places heavy demands on lateral balance.

[PUBLISHED] Walking speeds. VB2021: preferred speed 1.28 m/s (0.80-1.64), from a tail natural frequency of 0.66 Hz (0.41-0.84) and a 1.94 m step, with 'Trix' at 3.1 m hip height. F2026: about 1.5-2 m/s. Bellatoripes: 1.8-2.4 m/s. Glenrock trackway (40 cm tracks; sub-adult T. rex or Nanotyrannus): 2.2-3.5 m/s (Ruiz 2018, cited by F2026).

[PUBLISHED] Top speed. S2017 (BHI 3033 multibody model with bone-stress limits): true running with duty factor below 0.5 caused unacceptably high bone stress. At a 100 MPa limit the Froude number was 1.0, the walking limit; with stress unconstrained the model reached 7.7 m/s. HG2002: running at Fr 16 (about 20 m/s at a 2.5 m hip) would need about 43% of body mass as extensor muscle in each leg, against an expected 7-10%; maximum walking speed is about 5 m/s at Fr 1. The Field Museum's 'fast walk of 15 miles per hour' (6.7 m/s) is about Fr 1.5 at h = 3.1 m [derived comparison].

[DERIVED] Dimensionless gait targets. Preferred walk Fr = v^2/(g*h) is about 0.05 (0.02-0.09) from VB2021 and 0.07-0.13 from trackway speeds at h = 3.1 m. The walk-run limit is Fr about 1. Relative stride (stride divided by hip height) is about 1.2-1.3; VB2021 states that 'Bipedal dinosaurs seem to have preferred to walk at a relative stride length of 1.3'. Vertical hip or tail-base excursion in walking is about 0.08 m at a 3.1 m hip height, roughly 2.6%.

[DERIVED/INTERPRETIVE] Scaling to a robot under dynamic similarity (equal Froude number and relative stride): speed scales with sqrt(hip height) and step frequency with 1/sqrt(hip height). For example, a robot with a 1.0 m hip height matching 'Trix' (0.66 Hz and 1.28 m/s at 3.1 m) would step at about 1.16 Hz and walk at about 0.73 m/s, with a stride of about 1.25 m.

[PUBLISHED] Footprint shape. Tracks are functionally tridactyl and mesaxonic, with digit III longest. Digits are thick and taper to claws, with a broad metatarsal pad and sometimes a small hallux impression (MC2014; F2026 notes a possible pad or hallux at the rear of R2). Tyrannosauripus shows a posteromedially directed hallux. Track width/length is about 0.83 (F2026 R2) to 0.90 (Bellatoripes). Total divarication is 51-80°, with III-IV larger than II-III.

[PUBLISHED] Track sizes attributed to T. rex: Tyrannosauripus 86 cm, the Montana track 72 cm (Manning et al. 2008), and the North Dakota trackway about 0.9-1.0 m (F2026). Bellatoripes tracks are 52-67 cm and Glenrock 40 cm. F2026 cautions that tracks are probably larger than the foot.

[PUBLISHED] Hip height from footprint length. Alexander 1976 uses h about 4.0 x FL (as quoted by MC2014 and F2026; F2026 thus gets about 4 m for 1 m tracks, which they treat as indicative). MC2014's tyrannosaurid regression gives h/FL about 4.96 (2.87 m / 57.9 cm, derived). That regression uses leg length (femur + tibia + metatarsus +5%), i.e. a straight-limb hip height.

[PUBLISHED] Gait character. S2017's optimised, bone-stress-limited gaits kept vertical COM movement small, with no aerial phase, resembling bird-style 'grounded running'. VB2021 suggests the tail's natural frequency set the preferred stepping rhythm. [INTERPRETIVE] Aim for a compliant, grounded walk with a small vertical bounce and a passively oscillating tail, not an aerial run.
open_questions: Brochu 2003's measurement tables were not accessible. Plazi carries only the descriptive text, the T&F and JSTOR copies are paywalled, and the Plazi full-document XML returned 404. Sue's total skull length, MT III, pedal digit III phalanges, humerus and scapula length are therefore unverified. The only pedal value found is phalanx IV-1 at 154 mm (P2020).

Sue's skull length: 1.394 m comes only from Wikipedia, with no inline citation. CARR2020 states that senescent adults have skulls 'at least 1.4 m' long, with FMNH PR2081 as the single exemplar. GE2017's 127.5 cm uses a different landmark (posterior parietal margin). The skull on the Field Museum mount is a 'corrected cast'. Before scaling, decide which skull definition to use.

Hip height is used in at least three senses. The Field Museum's '13 ft at the hip' (3.96 m) probably measures to the top of the ilium. A derived check supports this: leg length 3.30 m plus about 0.55 m of ilium above the acetabulum (Sue ilium 1525 mm at Carr's adult ilium length/depth ratio of 2.8) gives about 3.85 m. H2011's 'leg length' is undefined; for Sue it exceeds femur + tibia + the adult MT III range by about 0.16-0.19 m. Model hip heights vary with posture (2.5-3.11 m). The robot spec needs an explicit acetabulum height for a chosen pose.

H2011 Tables 4-5: the limb segment masses sum with the axial segments exactly to the Table 6 whole-body masses (for example Stan: 4374 + 1560 = 5934 kg), and the fractions total about 100% only if each limb row is counted once. That implies the thigh, shank and foot rows cover both legs. Yet Table 9 and the text treat them as one hindlimb. Clarify before using H2011 per-leg masses; B2009 gives 14.4-16% per leg.

BHI 3033 femur: P2020 Table 1 gives 1350 mm, but H2011 gives 1.278 m from a scanned cast. Its tibia of 1065 mm (P2020) makes tibia/femur 0.79, an outlier. Check against the specimen or another source.

Persons et al. 2020 Table 1 values were read from Plazi's flattened text extraction. Column assignment was inferred because every numeric row resolves to exactly 12 cells, and it was cross-checked against PC2016 (CM 9380, MOR 555, RTMP 81.12.1), HS2003 (BHI 3033 dentary) and H2011 (MOR 555 femur). Still, verify against the published table before production use.

McCrea 2014 Table 1 prints a pace angulation of 117° for trackway A, but the text and the geometry indicate about 171°. Their quoted stride/hip-height ratio of 1.69 could not be reproduced (346/287 = 1.21; 346/230 = 1.50).

F2026 Table 1 (per-track and per-step metrics) is missing from the accepted manuscript, and the T&F version could not be fetched. Its CC-BY 3D scans (figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.31095802) would allow direct measurement of pace, stride, foot rotation, pace width and gauge. The trackway has only 4 poorly preserved tracks.

Skull width at the rear: HS2003 gives no total width, only nuchal crest widths. GE2017 width across the quadrates gives width/length 0.53-0.71, but the MOR 555 UCMP mount (PAD2022) gives 0.50, and that skull was reconstructed partly from MOR 008 casts. Which skull should the silhouette follow?
Neck length comes from a single reconstructed mount (PAD2022, MOR 555 cast, 180 cm along the S-curve). No other specimen's neck length or cervical measurements were accessible.

Fleshed chest and body widths are not tabulated in H2011, B2009 or SN2019. The only width data are qualitative or skeletal: Padian's 'well over a meter', the Field Museum's 44 in gastral span, and B2009's rule of about 18% of half-width as soft tissue.
Humerus/femur comes from one mount (MOR 555 cast at UCMP: 37 cm humerus). Sue's humerus length was not verified.
The 5-10° downward head pitch is secondary: Stevens' web page summarising a Science news item. The primary Witmer & Ridgely semicircular-canal study was not read.

Juvenile identity: Plazi lists Longrich & Saitta 2024 ('Nanotyrannus lancensis... a distinct taxon') and OpenAlex lists Zanno & Napoli 2025 in Nature ('Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus coexisted at the close of the Cretaceous'). Only the titles were seen. 'Jane' (BMRP 2002.4.1) and similar juveniles may not be T. rex, so juvenile ratios and ontogenetic trends should not be used for the robot without checking.

Speed figures conflict. The Field Museum's 15 mph 'fast walk' corresponds to about Fr 1.5, above the Fr ~1 walking limit used by S2017 and HG2002. HG2002's 'hip height roughly 2.5 m' belongs to their flexed running-pose model, not to a skeletal standing height.

Several full texts were not read; numbers from them came only from abstracts or quotations: Gatesy et al. 2009 (CC BY but blocked), Hutchinson et al. 2005 (joint angles and segment lengths), Persons & Currie 2011 (CFL and tail dimensions), Stevens 2006, Smith et al. 2016 (Glenrock), Manning et al. 2008, and Lockley & Hunt 1994.

Snively et al. 2019 Table 4: the swing-leg columns for the Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus rows look shifted (x values of 0.16-0.40 m, unlike other taxa), so they were not used. H2011 Table 8 prints BHI 3033's maximal CFL as '22' kg, probably a typo.
